### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via subDays (literal, a string literal in malformedNowAnchorRefusal))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbf7e04adff66aba72e634c65aae754440a8d89d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e2e30243cc3e812cb65ca84e0363e4dc3358d79b` — the merge of head `c7f0010efadca7f13953892ba37c139351f87209` into base `dbf7e04adff66aba72e634c65aae754440a8d89d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e2e30243cc3e812cb65ca84e0363e4dc3358d79b && git checkout e2e30243cc3e812cb65ca84e0363e4dc3358d79b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dbf7e04adff66aba72e634c65aae754440a8d89d c7f0010efadca7f13953892ba37c139351f87209 && git checkout -B drift-repro dbf7e04adff66aba72e634c65aae754440a8d89d && git merge --no-ff c7f0010efadca7f13953892ba37c139351f87209

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbf7e04adff66aba72e634c65aae754440a8d89d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dbf7e04adff66aba72e634c65aae754440a8d89d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c7f0010efadca7f13953892ba37c139351f87209`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-cross-field-comparison.ts (the dotted-offset refusal at lines 270, 352 and 517), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the aggregations[i].filter door near line 20456 and the having door near line 20539), packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts (assertAggregationFilterIsEvaluable), packages/formula/src/matches-filter.ts (resolveDayOffset, getPath), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts (the walk at line 413), packages/spec/src/data/filter.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.test.ts, skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md

Inputs read: card #26601 (body and all three comments: the seat ruling 6439436943, the claim 6439488124 and the os-dev report 6440958464), the governing records it names (maintainer ruling 6415710193 and the workload reading 6414128401 on #25808, the #14104 ruling 5507665791 and its correction 5550346132, the #15103 ruling 5548479553, and the prior contract review 6438749334 on #26592), PR #26655 (body, file list, net diff against main at this head) and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (the changeset, the three service-analytics test files and the two docs pages) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Check-runs at 2026-10-27T11:44Z. Complete and green: Lint & Repo Gates and every Lint lane, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Type Check source gates, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Test UI, Check PR Size, the PR-body guards and the docs link check. Still running: Build Core, all eight Test Core shards, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check debt ledger, Type Check UI and Build & E2E UI. Nothing had failed. The Temporal, opt-in and matrix-shard lanes are skipped, as this diff does not reach them. This record judges the design. The landing still waits for every required check to finish green, as the tier rule says.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept-set change at the shared walk. `judgeLiteralComparand` now routes a `{ $field }` reference and a well-formed now-anchor through `judgeAddDaysOffset`, which refuses when `addDays` is an object whose `$field` is a string containing a dot. Every other reference and anchor is still kept by reference. Read in the live tree, the predicate `ref.includes('.')` is the same one `driver-sql` uses at all three of its refusal sites, so the door refuses exactly the set the SQL read refuses. Right.

2. Which doors this reaches. `parseFilterAST` runs the walk on everything it returns, and the `FilterConditionSchema` save door goes through it, so data filters, dataset `filter` and dataset measure `filter` are covered. The engine runs the walk at the where door, at `aggregations[i].filter` (line 20456) and at `having` (line 20539). The RLS compiler runs it at line 413. The dev's door list is right, and one door short in its own favour again: the RLS seam refuses the shape too. No policy can carry an `addDays` today because the CEL compiler emits none, so the extra door changes nothing for a real caller. Right.

3. Order at the measure-filter door. At engine.ts the walk (line 20456) runs before `assertAggregationFilterIsEvaluable` (line 20457). So the dotted case is now answered by the walk, with the path and reason named, before the withheld sentence. That closes the card's "reason withheld" half without touching an executor. Right.

4. Accept-set change at the schema. `AddDaysReferenceSchema.$field` gains a regex refusing any dot, with the SQL sentence as its message. `FieldReferenceSchema.addDays` and `NowAnchorSchema.addDays` both use that schema, and the four ordering slots of `ComparisonOperatorSchema` and `FieldOperatorsSchema` use those two, so the refusal reaches every slot the pair and the anchor are legal in. `$eq` and `$ne` admit any comparand at the operator schema and are judged by the walk at the `FilterCondition` door. Right.

5. The issue path and message. In zod 4, when exactly one union option fails without aborting, that option's issues pass straight through. For a dotted offset the number option aborts on type and the object option fails only the regex, so the regex issue surfaces at `addDays.$field` with the custom sentence. The tests pin exactly that path. Right. A consequence is noted in ④.

6. JSON Schema projection. The rule is a regex, so the published JSON Schema carries it as a pattern and the dropped-refinement ledger does not grow. No committed artifact carries this schema: the json-schema manifest shards hold no `addDays`, the authorable-surface key set is unchanged (`data/FieldReference:addDays` already present), and no export is added or renamed, so api-surface does not move. The one describe change is regenerated into `content/docs/references/data/filter.mdx`. Right.

7. Executors unchanged and consistent. `driver-sql` already refuses the shape at lines 352 and 517. `having-filter.ts` keeps its own class rules for the offset column. The formula evaluator's `resolveDayOffset` walks the path with `getPath`; on a stored row where the lookup holds an id string, `getPath` returns undefined at the second segment, the offset reads as zero days, and the comparison runs. I confirmed that reading in the code. So before this change the only executor that accepted the shape answered it wrong on a stored row. Refusing it at every door restores the #14104 ruling's own premise that the offset evaluates identically on both paths. Right.

8. The base `$field` keeps its asymmetry. A dotted base reference such as `{ $field: 'duty.due_on' }` still validates everywhere, memory walks it and SQL refuses it. The PR names this, pins it as a control, and leaves it outside the card's order. Right, and the right carrier.

9. Public surface. `dottedAddDaysOffset`, `dottedAddDaysOffsetRefusal`, `judgeAddDaysOffset`, `dottedAddDaysReference` and `dottedAddDaysOffsetSentence` are module-private. The refusal reuses `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. Right.

10. The two should-fixes carried from review 6438749334 are taken: the subDays clause prints only when `subDays` is among the undeclared keys, and the stale `isNowAnchor` docblock sentence now names the walk. Both are pinned. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor`. Right.

- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is measured: `FieldReferenceSchema`, `NowAnchorSchema`, the ordering slots, `FilterConditionSchema`, `DatasetSchema` and `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` all accepted `addDays: { $field: 'a.b' }` on base, and each refuses it now. A filter is something a metadata author writes. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 makes a declared kind at least `minor` on the package the diff moves.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` matches the diff. Nothing widens. The PR body and the changeset carry the same value and the same arm.
- The BREAKING banner, the `fix(spec)!:` title and one ADR-0087 marker reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` are present in the changeset body. The disposition is sound: no key is added, removed or renamed, and there is no mechanical rewrite that keeps what the author meant, because the related value has to be copied onto a column of the row. The changeset states the remedy. Check Changeset is green on the head.
- service-analytics, objectql, formula and the docs pages change tests or prose only and publish nothing. No second changeset owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The seat ruling's "every SQL read refuses" framing against the memory path. The memory evaluator does not refuse a dotted offset, it walks it. The dev measured what it answers on a stored row: zero days, silently. That is the silent-wrong-answer class Prime Directive 10 names, and Prime Directive 12 says to reject at authoring what the runtime cannot deliver. The narrowing is sound on both grounds, not only on the SQL one. Closed.
- Naming the #14104 correction 5550346132 as superseded. The brief asked for this judgment. The record has two parts. Its corrected example, the same-table spelling with every column on the object the filter runs over, is unchanged and is precisely what this PR enforces. Its boundary sentence ("answered by the memory evaluator and refused by SQL push-down") was a measurement of the code at the time, written by a seat under the #15103 fallback B, which the maintainer ruled as "capability unchanged" for SQL. The maintainer never ruled that the memory path must keep answering the dotted spelling. So what this PR retires is one sentence of that record, at the authoring doors, on the strength of the #25808 ruling A (same-record column) and the measured silent answer. That is sound. Calling the whole record superseded is not: the record's corrected example stands. The changeset says "retires the earlier reading", which is scoped right. The PR body heads it "Superseded readings" and names the record. should-fix on the prose, for the adopting seat: a one-line pointer under 5550346132 on #14104 saying its boundary sentence is narrowed by this PR, with no rewrite of the record. Not a code change and not a FAIL.
- Does a seat have the word to narrow the pair form, not only the now-anchor? The maintainer's #14104 ruling A (5507665791) named the dotted spelling as its example. The maintainer's #15103 ruling (5548479553) then said in advance that under fallback B the example is corrected to the same-table form "so the ruling no longer teaches a refused shape", and the correction did that. The maintainer's #25808 ruling A (6415710193) bounds the anchor offset to a column of the same record and says both standing rulings hold. So no maintainer word teaches the dotted offset any more, and the seat's dispatch of the author-time refusal reverses none. The BREAKING changeset carries the change in the open. Closed.
- Files beyond the claimed two, each named to the seat before the edit: three service-analytics test files, query-syntax.mdx and the regenerated filter.mdx. Read: the three tests flip their save-door assertion to the refusal and keep the read-time pin by putting the dotted filter back past the door with a typed spread. That is the right way to pin a row that never met the door. Closed.
- The bare implicit form `{ field: { $field, addDays } }` is not judged. The walk steps around it whole, as it did before, and #7597 owns its fate. Pinned as a control. Not escalated.
- `Skills-docs: none`. filters.md line 72 already teaches the offset as a number field of the same record, and line 80 says SQL push-down refuses a dotted offset. Both sentences stay true. The sentence could now also list "a dotted offset" among the 400 refusals; that is a one-word edit on a governed surface and belongs in its own PR. Not escalated.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: the other withheld refusals at `aggregations[i].filter` (an undeclared, non-numeric or tenant offset column) stay withheld. Read in having-filter.ts, that is the existing design of that door and not a pass-through in a touched file. A note in the acceptance notes is the right carrier. Not escalated.
- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing left to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts

The scenario: an author writes a dataset measure filter whose `addDays` offset reads `contract_type.review_sla_days`, runs `os validate`, and gets green gates and a tile that errors on every read. After this change, `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` refuses the stack at the slot, in the sentence the SQL read would have used. I tried to break it along these lines.

- Predicate agreement. The walk, the schema and `driver-sql` all ask whether the string contains a dot. There is no shape the walk refuses that an executor would have compiled, and none it keeps that SQL refuses on this rule. Good.
- Both carriers. The pair and the anchor share `judgeAddDaysOffset`, and the anchor's well-formed check runs first, so a malformed anchor still gets its own sentence and a well-formed one with a dotted offset gets this one. The resolved anchor form the engine hands the executors is judged the same way and pinned. Good.
- Copy-on-write contract. The new branch answers keep or refuse and never narrows, so a kept reference is still the same object. The control test pins it for five shapes. Good.
- Refusal length. The sentence at the measure-filter position under the engine prefix, with a long field and a long offset path, is pinned at or under 500 characters with the "NOT applied" tail intact. `preview` bounds the offset path at 40 characters. Good.
- Non-string `$field` on the offset. `{ addDays: { $field: 123 } }` is kept by the walk and refused by the schema's own union sentence at the save door. Same as before this change. Not a finding.
- Empty `$field` on the offset. `addDays: { $field: '' }` passes the regex and the walk. On base, `z.string()` accepted it too, so this is not a regression; SQL refuses it as an undeclared column and memory reads it as zero days. Outside this card. Not a finding.

No must-fix.

packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts

- The regex on `AddDaysReferenceSchema.$field` is the right instrument: it projects to JSON Schema and keeps the refinement ledger flat. Its custom message is the SQL sentence plus the same-record prescription, and the tests pin that the message carries no tracker number. Good.
- The docblock at the top of the file now states the same-record bound and names the retired reading in one place; the ordering-slot docblock repeats it in one sentence. Consistent with the walk's module note. Good.
- should-fix: the new `dotted` arm at the top of `addDaysOffsetMessage` is not reached by any pinned path. Under zod 4's single-option pass-through, a dotted offset surfaces as the regex's own issue at `addDays.$field`, and `fieldReferenceIssueMessage` reparses through `FieldReferenceSchema` and returns that same issue. The union's custom error is consulted only when no option or more than one option fails without aborting, which a dotted offset does not produce. Either pin a case that reaches the arm, or drop it and let the regex sentence be the one source. Not a must-fix: no door answers wrong, and the surfaced message is the right one.
- The two spellings of the sentence, the walk's and the schema's, differ in case and punctuation only and are both pinned against the driver's wording. Acceptable, and the docblock says why there are two.

No must-fix. The tree does what the seat ruling dispatched: a dotted offset the runtime refuses is refused at save and validate time, with the reason named, and nothing is widened.
